2026-09-18T13:58:32+00:00  RULING OBS-17 CLOSED, PASS. The auditor reproduced 36950.00 and confirmed the route is real but not defensible, and put on the record what carries the exclusion rather than leaving it to inference: (1) a sentence in the clause that performs the subtraction lists payments, credit memos and discounts as three coordinate heads, so reaching 36950.00 means deducting one row under two of them, 1155.00 in all, for a row that moved 1016.40 — a misapplication of an unambiguous sentence, not a second reading; (2) summing the ledger reproduces balance_after at all 14 rows and the credit memo moves it by exactly -1016.40, checkable from records alone; (3) the discount enumeration excludes a restocking charge, the returns arithmetic identifies the figure as 12% of the extended amount, the discount rows carry a type the credit memo lacks, and the figure is withheld FROM the member so 'discount granted' inverts the sign. It also found a FOURTH route to the same number that the referral had missed, reaching it without any discount misreading, and showed it fails a step earlier and is foreclosed by the same ledger leg.
2026-09-18T13:58:32+00:00  LIMIT-ON-RECORD from that ruling: the protection is STRUCTURAL, not lexical — it holds because the credit-memo term sits in the same sentence as the discount term. Separate those terms, drop the credit-memo term, or add a task-0-side binding that subtracts discounts without credit memos, and the bar vanishes and OBS-17 reopens on that binding.
